chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Marwak, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the people of quenching (drinking) in the world from the intoxicant die thirsty, and are resurrected thirsty, and enter the Fire thirsty.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of drinking intoxicants according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni narrates this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that the 'thirst' of wine drinkers is not merely physical but a spiritual deprivation resulting from the loss of divine proximity. This tripartite thirst—occurring at death, resurrection, and in Hell—reflects the Shia scholarly view that intoxicants cloud the heart, preventing the soul from quenching its thirst for God with the 'wine' of divine knowledge. The hadith thus serves as a warning that the temporary euphoria of khamr leads to eternal longing and exclusion from the ultimate reward.
